citations.quote: An **admissible constraint class** is a nonempty subset $C\subseteq U$; its constrained forward map is the restriction $A|_C:C\to Y$. The class $C$ is **identifiable for $A$** if $A|_C$ is injective, meaning $Ax=Ax'$ for $x,x'\in C$ implies $x=x'$. Define the difference set and kernel by $$C-C:=\{x-x':x,x'\in C\},\qquad \ker A:=\{x\in X:Ax=0_Y\}.$$
A function $T:V\to W$ is **linear** when $$T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)$$ for all $a,b\in F$ and $u,v\in V$.
For a linear map $T:V\to W$, its **kernel** and **image** are respectively $$\ker T:=\{v\in V:T(v)=0_W\},\qquad \operatorname{im}T:=\{T(v):v\in V\}.$$

derivations.claim: A difference that lies in the kernel identifies its two endpoints; injectivity forces the difference to be zero, and nonemptiness supplies zero in the intersection.
Equal forward data make the difference of two constrained truths lie in both the difference set and the kernel, so the assumed trivial intersection forces equality.

boundaries.evidence: If C were empty, A restricted to C would be vacuously injective while C-C and its kernel intersection would be empty; the nonempty hypothesis is essential. See step 1.1.
For a singleton C, C-C={0}; the intersection is {0} and the restricted map is injective. See step 1.1.

boundaries.reason: The proposition has no scalar threshold or unit parameter.

boundaries.evidence: For A=0, ker A=X and the condition reduces to C-C={0}, equivalent to C being a singleton and hence to injectivity of the constant restriction. See step 1.1.

boundaries.reason: There is no interval or boundary parameter.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 selects one element from the assumed nonempty C only to witness 0 in C-C; no choice axiom or family selection is used.

citations.quote: Set the current frame to $X_0$ and the schedule index to $k=0$. If $r(X)\le\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$. 2. While $k<K$, compute $G(X)$ and the Stiefel gradient $g:=G(X)-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G(X))$. If $g=0$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{stationary})$.

Evaluate $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})$ and $r(X_{\rm trial})$. If $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})>\Phi(X)$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{objective-rejected})$. Otherwise accept $X_{\rm trial}$ as the current frame. If its residual is at most $\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$; otherwise increment $k$ by one and repeat the loop. 5. When $k=K$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{budget-exhausted})$.

For $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, the tangent space and its Frobenius orthogonal projection are $$T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)=\{Z:X^{\mathsf T}Z+Z^{\mathsf T}X=0\},\qquad \Pi_X^{\rm St}(G)=G-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G).$$

On the full-column-rank domains of [[def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions]], the positive-diagonal QR and polar maps are smooth, take values in $\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, fix $\eta=0$, and have differential $D R_X(0)[\eta]=\eta$.

derivations.claim: The symmetric-part subtraction makes the Stiefel gradient tangent, and positive scalar multiplication preserves tangency.
Each trial from a feasible frame is polar-retracted to another feasible frame, so accepted iterates remain feasible by finite induction.
The bounded index loop returns within K trials; every successful status and every accepted objective update match the explicit branch checks.

boundaries.reason: The procedure requires an initial frame X0 in St(n,p), so an empty feasible set is excluded by its input.

boundaries.evidence: If the initial residual is zero and tau=0, the first residual check returns target-met without a trial. This is the zero-residual branch in the Statement.

For p=1 the Stiefel set is the unit sphere; the tangent projection and polar retraction formulas remain defined on its tangent inputs. The Statement permits p=1 and uses the same tangent formula in step 1.1.
A zero projected gradient returns stationary when the residual test has failed; the procedure makes no minimum claim. See step 3.1.
At K=0, the initial residual is tested and the procedure otherwise returns budget-exhausted; every scheduled alpha is strictly positive. See step 3.1.
The procedure uses only its supplied initial frame and finite schedule and makes no selection from an arbitrary family. The finite procedure in the Statement makes no selections.
